title: De-Googling
subtitle: Google's products are deeply embedded in most people's digital lives, but each one collects a significant amount of your personal data. This guide walks through switching off Google's data collection and replacing products with privacy-focused alternatives.

context.title: You don't have to do this all at once
context.body: De-Googling your life is a slow and sometimes painful process. It's not reasonable for most people to eliminate Google entirely, so many of these recommendations assume you're keeping your Google account. Partially de-Googling is better than nothing.
context.body2: Check out our guides on web browsers and search engines for detailed comparison tables if you wish to learn more about any of the software we list below.

warning.body: Removing Google from your life is one of the more difficult tasks because it's in every aspect of our daily lives. From your browser, to your search engine, to services like YouTube, it's basically everywhere. Giving up some of their services will require some adjustment, but with time it'll be easier to erase them from your life.

items.name: Personal info
items.why: Google stores a detailed log of everything you do across its products. This data is used for ad targeting and is stored unless you turn it off.

steps.text: Go `myaccount.google.com` → `Personal info`
Change your profile picture to something anonymous
Change your display name
`Gender` → change to `Rather not say` → toggle on `Only me`
`Email` → `Manage About me emails` → make sure `Gender`, `Birthday`, `Email`, and `Mobile` are set to `Only Me`
`Home address` → remove
`Work address` → remove
`Other addresses` → remove any addresses that aren't your legal address

items.name: Security & sign-in
items.why: These settings will help your overall account security.

steps.text: Enable `2-Step Verification` → use an authenticator app
Enable `Passkeys and security keys` → use the passkey feature in a password manager or use a physical security key like Yubikey
Ensure you have a recovery phone and email configured
`Your linked apps` → disconnect Google login for all apps - be sure to change how you log in to those apps before disconnecting Google
Toggle off `Enhanced Safe Browsing for your account`

items.name: Data & privacy
items.why: Google stores a detailed log of everything you do across its products. This data is used for ad targeting and is stored indefinitely unless you turn it off.

steps.text: Go `myaccount.google.com` → `Data & privacy`
Toggle off `Personalize Search`
Toggle off `Personalize Google Play`
Pause `Web & App Activity`
Toggle off `Google Play History`
Toggle off `YouTube History`
Pause `Timeline`

items.name: People & sharing
items.why: Limit how much information is shared in Google services.

steps.text: Go `myaccount.google.com` → `People & sharing`
Toggle off `Contact info from your devices`
Audit items listed in `Location sharing`
Audit items listed in `About me`
Toggle off `Business personalization`
Toggle off `Shared endorsements in ads`

items.name: Disable Gemini & AI features
items.why: Google's Gemini features are integrated across all of their services. By default, your conversations with Gemini are stored and used to train Google's AI models.

steps.text: Go to `myaccount.google.com` → `Gemini`
In Gmail: click the Gemini icon → `Settings` → `Turn off Gemini in Gmail`
On Android: `Settings` → `Google` → `All Services` → `Gemini` and disable
Check `myaccount.google.com` → `Data & privacy` → `AI features` for any remaining AI activity controls

items.name: Replace Gmail
items.why: Google scans the content of everyone's Gmail and Drive. Many people keep sensitive documents in their inboxes to refer to later, or they don't consider deleting files after they've been downloaded. There are some popular alternatives making their way into the mainstream that might make good alternatives to Gmail.

steps.text: `Proton` - likely the most popular privacy-focused email service. They offer both free and paid tiers. This is one of the few alternatives that offers an entire suite of products that can be used to replace Google. Sign up at `https://mail.proton.me`

`Tuta` - an up and coming service that also offers free and paid tiers. Their Drive is currently in beta testing, so expect that to be available in the near future. Sign up at `https://tuta.com/secure-email`

items.name: Ditch Chrome
items.why: Chrome sends your browsing behavior to Google, logs your history if signed into a Google account, and they've disabled full ad-blocking via Manifest V3. Switching to a different browser facilitates the largest reduction in Google's visibility into your web activity. See our Browsers guide for more a detailed comparison.

steps.text: Download Firefox (`mozilla.org/firefox`) or Brave (`brave.com`)
Export Chrome bookmarks: `3 dot menu` → `Bookmarks and lists` → `Bookmark manager` → `3 dot menu on pop out` → `Export bookmarks`
Import bookmarks on Firefox: `Menu` → `Bookmarks` → `Manage bookmarks` → `up / down arrows` → `Import bookmarks from HTML`
Import bookmarks on Brave: `Menu` → `Bookmarks and lists` → `Import bookmarks and settings`
Set as your default browser in your computer's system settings

items.name: Replace Google Search
items.why: Every query you enter in Google Search is linked to your account or a persistent identifier. Over years this builds an extraordinarily detailed picture of your life and personal details.

steps.text: In Firefox: `Settings` → `Search` → `Default Search Engine` → choose your preferred search engine
In Brave: `Settings` → `Search engine` → choose your preferred search engine
On iOS: `Settings` → `Apps` → `Safari` → `Search Engine` → choose your preferred search engine
On Android: Open your preferred browser → tap on the search engine icon in the search bar → `Search settings` → `Default search engine` → choose your preferred search engine

items.name: Replace Google Maps
items.why: Google Maps builds a detailed picture of everywhere you go - your home, workplace, doctor's office, places of worship, political events. This location history can be subpoenaed.

steps.text: `Apple Maps` - a significant privacy improvement over Google Maps. Apple doesn't build a location history profile. Available on iPhone and Mac
`OsmAnd` - open source, uses OpenStreetMap data, fully offline capable. No account required, no tracking. iOS and Android
`Organic Maps` - simpler than OsmAnd, excellent for offline use, no ads or tracking

items.name: Replace Google Drive
items.why: Google Drive and Docs store your documents on Google's servers - accessible to Google and subject to legal requests. Every document you write in Google Docs is potentially readable by Google.

steps.text: `Proton Drive` - E2EE cloud word processor. Part of the Proton ecosystem. Free tier is available with very limited storage
`CryptPad` - E2EE office suite with free and paid tiers. Open source, no account needed
`LibreOffice` - free, open source desktop office suite with comparable capabilities to Google
`Grist` - open source spreadsheet service with self-hosting option. Replaces Google Sheets

items.name: Replace Google Calendar
items.why: A good calendar app is hard to come by, but not impossible to find. The below options are a few that offer features that you come to expect like sync, sharing, and notifications.

steps.text: FINISH
FINISH
FINISH
FINISH
`Jitsi` - a free video conferencing tool that you can use directly in the web or self-host. Check it out at `https://jitsi.org/`
FINISH

items.name: Stop using 'Sign in with Google' on websites
items.path: Applies to all websites and apps
items.why: Every time you use 'Sign in with Google,' you're telling Google which service you're using, when, and how often.

steps.text: Go to `myaccount.google.com` → `Security` → `Third-party apps with account access` and review every connected app
For each app, create a standalone account using an email address instead, then revoke the Google connection
Going forward: always choose 'Sign up with email' over 'Continue with Google' - use Firefox Relay or Apple Hide My Email to keep your real address private

items.name: Replace Google Photos with a private alternative
items.why: Google Photos uses AI to analyze every photo you upload - identifying faces, locations, objects, and events. This analysis builds an extremely detailed profile of your life, relationships, and whereabouts.

steps.text: `Apple Photos with Advanced Data Protection` - end-to-end encrypted. Best for iPhone users
`Ente Photos` - open source, E2EE photo storage with apps for iOS, Android, and desktop. Designed as a Google Photos replacement
`Local storage` - store photos on your device only and back up to an encrypted external drive. Recommended for tech savvy users who know how to set up redundant backups

items.name: Download your Google data, then request deletion
items.path: takeout.google.com → myaccount.google.com → Delete your Google Account
items.why: If you're ready to fully leave Google, deleting your account removes Google's ability to retain your historical data.

steps.text: Go to `takeout.google.com` - select all products and request a download if you wish to keep a copy. Google will email you when the archive is ready (may take hours or days)
Confirmed you've migrated all important services off Google first like Gmail, Drive, Photos, and any apps that use Google to login
Go to `myaccount.google.com` → `Data & privacy` → `Delete your Google Account`
